USER: create the most realistic and accurate 3D model of the taj majal (with surrounding scenery). build a camera system to allow free view inspection of the model.

Put it all together in the end with a 20 second showcase in a very impressive way. You will be the director of that 20 second showcase, make the most of it, make it cinematic, and most of all make no mistakes.

content.thinking:
The user wants an extremely realistic and accurate 3D model of the Taj Mahal with surrounding scenery, plus a camera system for free view inspection, and a 20‑second cinematic showcase directed by me. I need to outline how I'm going to approach this. First, I should decide on the technology stack. Since the user didn't specify any particular platform, a web‑based solution using Three.js is the most accessible and can be run directly in the browser, satisfying the “self‑contained” requirement. Three.js also provides built‑in geometry, material, lighting, and camera controls that I can extend for a dual‑mode system (orbit for inspection and a fly‑through for the cinematic).

Next, I need to think about the components of the model. The Taj Mahal is complex: a large plinth, the main central dome (onion shape), four smaller domes, chhatris, minarets, the mosque and jawab wings, the great gate, and the surrounding Char‑Bāgh garden with its reflecting pool and pathways. To keep the solution manageable yet realistic, I’ll describe these parts as procedurally generated meshes (using BoxGeometry, CylinderGeometry, TorusKnotGeometry, etc.) with appropriate scaling and positioning. I’ll note the key architectural elements (pishtaq facades, the intricate arches, the marble texture) and mention that I’ll apply high‑resolution textures or PBR materials to approximate the marble look.

The camera system should allow free inspection, so I’ll combine an OrbitControls instance (for rotating around the model) with a custom FlyControls mode that can be toggled. I’ll need to explain that I’ll implement a simple UI button or key press to switch between these modes.

Finally, the 20‑second showcase needs a script: start with a wide establishing shot of the whole complex, then a smooth dolly‑in toward the main dome, a fly‑through over the garden, a circling orbit around the minarets, and end with a dramatic pull‑back to reveal the full site. I’ll state that I’ll orchestrate this with a sequence of camera keyframes and possibly use GSAP or a custom animation loop.

Before I dive into writing any code, I should verify the current workspace – there may already be some files or a project skeleton present. So I’ll let the user know my plan (self‑contained Three.js app with procedural Taj Mahal, dual‑mode camera, and scripted showcase) and then say I’ll check the workspace first. This response directly addresses the user’s request and sets up the next logical step.
I'll build this as a self-contained Three.js app: a procedurally modeled Taj Mahal (plinth, pishtaq facades, onion dome, chhatris, minarets, mosque & jawab, great gate, charbagh gardens with reflecting pool), a dual-mode camera system (orbit + fly), and a scripted 20-second cinematic showcase.
